messages:
Aisha Patel: FYI a customer (acme-analytics) opened a ticket — they suddenly started seeing a bunch of 429s and elevated tail latency after a feature flag flip yesterday. They say it coincided with a rollout but unsure which route/model. Ticket: https://support.redwood.example/tickets/4521
Tom Nguyen: Can you paste a sample request id or error payload? Also, which API key/client_id are they using?
Aisha Patel: From the ticket: 
```
{\n  status: 429,\n  code: \"rate_limit\",\n  message: \"burst limit exceeded\",\n  request_id: \"req_0a1b2c3d\"\n}
```
Client mentions key prefix acct-7gH and they were calling /v1/generate with model=redwood-7b:quantized. The spike started at ~2025-11-03T14:02Z.
Jules Mercado: OK, first triage: we need to attribute the 429 to (a) route config, (b) per-customer quota exhaustion, (c) autoscaling gap, or (d) upstream retries causing bursts. Run these queries in the observability cluster:
1) route-level 429 rate (1m) by route and model: 
```
SELECT route, model, sum(status_code=429) AS count_429, sum(requests) AS total
FROM metrics.http_requests
WHERE ts BETWEEN now()-1h AND now()
GROUP BY route, model
ORDER BY count_429 DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
2) customer quota consumption: 
```
SELECT customer_id, sum(tokens) as tokens_used, max(burst_used) as peak_burst
FROM usage.billing_windows
WHERE window_start >= date_trunc('hour', now()-2h)
AND customer_id = 'acct-7gH'
GROUP BY customer_id;
```
Kai Rivera: I also want KV cache hitrate and latency by model variant. If the model variant switched to quantized with lower cache efficiency, that can increase per-token latency and cause clients to retry. Quick check: 
```
metrics.kv_cache_hits{model=~\"redwood-.*\"} by (model)
```
Aisha Patel: Ran query #1, got this (snip): 
```
route: /v1/generate, model: redwood-7b:quant -> count_429: 312, total: 4200
route: /v1/stream, model: redwood-7b -> count_429: 3, total: 900
```
So 99% of 429s are on /v1/generate for the quantized variant.
Tom Nguyen: That strongly suggests either per-route or per-model throttles engaged for that variant. Check route config: /configs/rate-limits.yaml for that customer tier. Also check if they were recently switched to a lower plan or had a quota reset.
quota-bot: Customer acct-7gH consumed 1.8M tokens in the last 2h, burst allowance used: 100% of daily burst pool.
Jules Mercado: Aha — full daily burst exhausted. Two notes: (1) attribute is mostly quota exhaustion, not autoscale gap. (2) need to know whether requests came in short bursts (sustained high QPS) or many concurrent small requests. Pull the distribution of requests per-min: 
```
SELECT floor(ts/60) AS minute, count(*) as hits
FROM requests
WHERE customer_id='acct-7gH' AND ts >= now()-2h
GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute;
```
Kai Rivera: Also correlate with client-side retry patterns. If they had aggressive retries with no jitter, that amplifies bursts. Ask them for SDK version and whether they use exponential backoff.
Aisha Patel: I asked the customer; they said they deployed a change that splits a single bulk call into 6 parallel calls to speed up perceived latency. They also disabled retries at the SDK level. That produced a short-lived QPS spike.
Tom Nguyen: That explains it — parallel fanout + burst pool exhausted -> 429s. For observability improvements, I propose: 
- Add a dashboard panel that shows per-customer burst pool usage (counter + % of pool) with a 5m and 1h rollup.
- Add per-route 429 attribution by model variant and include sample request_ids.
- Alert: fire when a customer's burst pool > 85% for 10m OR 429 rate for that customer > 5% of requests for 5m.
Jules Mercado: Agreed. Implementation notes: store burst pool usage in the billing pipeline (we already emit bursts but not in the default support dashboard). Create a Grafana panel: datasource=metrics-store, query=usage.burst_pool_by_customer. Make a templated dashboard with customer_id variable.
Kai Rivera: Short-term mitigation options for the customer: (1) temporarily increase their burst allowance (manual escalation or support API), (2) recommend they roll back the parallelization or add jitter/backoff, (3) route them to a compatible non-quantized variant if it handles bursts better.
Aisha Patel: Customer requested immediate relief. I increased their burst pool by +30% for 1 hour and asked them to throttle client. They accepted rollback plan.
Tom Nguyen: For runbook updates: add a step to check `usage.burst_pool_by_customer` and `route.429_by_model` as the first two checks. Include quick queries in the runbook and a playbook action to temporarily change burst_kv for a customer via admin UI or `support://adjust-burst`.
Jules Mercado: I'll create the dashboard and alert, and add the queries to the shared runbook. Also adding a tiny helper that links each 429 to the originating model variant and request_id so support can quickly open a timeline. Patch notes: 
- dashboard: Support -> Limits -> Per-customer burst usage (new)
- alert: CustomerBurstHigh (threshold 85% for 10m) -> notify #support and #eng-runtime
- runbook: updated with queries and mitigation steps
Kai Rivera: One extra telemetry idea: include a small sampling of the full request payload (sanitized) in the logging pipeline for high-severity 429s so we can see whether payloads are large / causing token spikes. Limit to 1% sample to control cost.
Aisha Patel: Thanks team. I'll close the ticket after confirming the customer rolled back and 429s stayed down for 30m. Leaving here for follow-up: add incident tags, link dashboard, and update ticket with next steps + recommended SDK backoff config.
Tom Nguyen: Thx — once dashboard is live, tag me and I'll validate the alert thresholds.
Jules Mercado: Will do. Created internal task INF-879 to track dashboard/alert/runbook changes.
quota-bot: Note: automatic rebalancer will run at 01:00 UTC — any temporary manual increments will be reverted unless flagged persistent.
Aisha Patel: Noted. I'll set a persistent flag if customer wants longer-term increase after billing review.
Tom Nguyen: Closing loop: root cause = client-side parallelization + burst pool exhaustion. Observability gap = no per-customer burst panel and no alert at 85% pool. Resolved by temporary burst increase + dashboard + runbook update.
Aisha Patel: Closing ticket once I confirm no regressions. :+1:
